Article Title: 'Serious setback': Ex-Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah on HC's move to strike down 56% quota
Article Text:
Siddaramaiah calls Karnataka HC’s 56% quota ruling a “serious setback”; Parameshwara hints at SC appeal.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah on Monday termed the Karnataka high court’s decision to strike down the law enhancing reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) a “serious setback” to historically marginalised communities.The law raised SC reservation from 15% to 17% and ST reservation from 3% to 7%, taking the combined quota beyond the 50% ceiling."We respect the judiciary. However, the judgment raises fundamental questions about the BJP's handling of social justice. The BJP government increased SC reservation from 15% to 17% and ST reservation from 3% to 7% ahead of the 2023 assembly elections, despite knowing that total reservation would exceed the 50% ceiling," news agency ANI quoted Siddaramaiah as saying."Why did the BJP announce enhanced reservation without first ensuring its constitutional sustainability? Was electoral advantage prioritised over lasting social justice?" he added.He said the demand followed “decades of struggle” and criticised the Centre for deferring Karnataka’s request to include the enhanced quotas in the Constitution’s Ninth Schedule.“Reservation is not charity,” Siddaramaiah said, calling for a review of the 50% ceiling and urging the state government to pursue legal remedies.Deputy chief minister G Parameshwara also described the ruling as a “serious development with far-reaching implications” for education and public employment.He questioned the previous BJP government’s decision to enact the law in October 2022 and criticised the Centre for delaying a decision on the Ninth Schedule proposal.Parameshwara said the state government “will examine all available legal remedies, including an appeal before the Hon'ble Supreme Court”. He added that Dalit and Adivasi children must inherit “greater opportunities, not prolonged legal uncertainty”.
Article Summary: Siddaramaiah calls Karnataka HC’s 56% quota ruling a “serious setback”; Parameshwara hints at SC appeal. Law raised SC reservation from 15% to 17% and ST reservation from 3% to 7%.

Article Title: 6 killed, several injured as passenger train derails in Pakistan's Punjab
Article Text:
Train travelling from Karachi to Peshawar derails in Pakistan (Representative image) (PTI)

At least six people were killed and several others injured after a passenger train derailed in Pakistan's Punjab province early Tuesday, Pakistan-based Geo News reported.The Rehman Baba Express, travelling from the southern port city of Karachi to the northwestern city of Peshawar, derailed in Sher Shah, Punjab province, news agency AP reported, citing Pakistan Railways spokesperson Kaleem Akhtar.The injured were taken to Nishtar Hospital in Multan for treatment, while rescue teams continued operations at the accident site.The accident took place at around 5.15am, according to Geo News.Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed grief over the deaths in separate statements and directed authorities to ensure the best possible medical care for the injured.Train accidents are relatively common in Pakistan, where the railway system has suffered from decades of underinvestment, outdated tracks and ageing signalling systems.In 2023, 10 carriages of a passenger train derailed in southern Pakistan, killing 30 people and injuring more than 90 others.
Article Summary: Passenger train travelling from Karachi to Peshawar derails in Pakistan. At least six people killed and several others injured in Sher Shah, Punjab province. Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif express grief over the deaths.

Article Title: 'When did hoisting tricolour become violation?' Abhijeet Dipke questions Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka's detention at Jantar Mantar
Article Text:
‘Jantar Mantar belongs to people’: CJP’s Dipke slams crackdown on protesters

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke on Tuesday hit out at the Centre after several members of his team were detained in Delhi, calling those who consider hoisting the national flag at Jantar Mantar a violation of the law "traitors"."Our team went to Jantar Mantar this morning and hoisted the tricolor. When did hoisting the tricolor become a violation? Whoever thinks that hoisting the tricolor at Jantar Mantar is a violation is a traitor. And if Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde, and the others who were arrested for hoisting the tricolor are charged, then there should be strict action taken against it. How can you arrest someone for hoisting the tricolor? What kind of country is this? What kind of rule is this?" Dipke questioned.Addressing the police action, he cautioned against denying legal rights to those in custody."The whole country will become Jantar Mantar. Jantar Mantar is not just a location; it is a spirit of resistance," Dipke said. "We hope that the Delhi Police will let them talk to their lawyers. It shouldn't happen that, as it happened to me, they are kept for 24 hours without being allowed to speak to a lawyer. As a legal procedure, they should be allowed to speak to a lawyer because you cannot just pick someone up like this."The CJP leader further described the crackdown as the "greatest example of a dictatorial mentality", alleging that the government was treating public spaces as its private domain."The dictatorship doesn't want anyone to go to Jantar Mantar and hoist the tricolor. They think the whole country is their personal property. It is not like that; Jantar Mantar belongs to the people of this country, the 140 crore Indians," he added.Dipke vowed to continue the agitation until their demand was met. "We will hoist the tricolor there, and we will keep hoisting it until Jyanesh Kumar resigns," he said.Dipke’s remarks came after Delhi Police detained his colleagues, including Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya Shinde, who had gathered at Jantar Mantar earlier on Tuesday.The group began its demonstration in the early hours of the morning, but security personnel took the protesters into custody shortly after they arrived at the site.According to an official notice, Delhi Police on Monday removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest venues and named three alternative locations for demonstrations: Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi.The notice said the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) had constituted a committee to identify alternative venues where citizens could exercise their right to organise protests. Based on the committee’s recommendations, Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a designated protest site.

Article Title: As Jantar Mantar loses protest site tag, CJP plans get disrupted
Article Text:
The CJP leaders recently approached the Delhi Police to organize a protest addressing issues with the electoral roll

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Monday gave Delhi Police 24 hours to set a date for its proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against alleged electoral roll revision irregularities, offering the force the choice to decide when it could be held.However, just as the green light was sought, police announced the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, throwing CJP's plan into uncertainty and prompting it to slam the move.Hours before party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka came to Parliament Street police station to submit a letter regarding its demand, barricades and security personnel had taken over adjacent roads.Even Firoz Shah Road, around 10 minutes away, had barricades and police personnel stationed along it.Closer to Parliament Street, access was restricted, with loudspeakers repeatedly warning: "Section 163 of BNSS is in place. Please abide by law and order. Stay away from barricades on the road." Just outside the police station, security was even tighter, with announcements also spelling out restrictions for media personnel.Ranka said, "We have come to police with a letter giving them the option to suggest a date on which we can hold our protest.The DCP came into the room, but left when he saw us sitting there. So, we could not meet him. The additional DCP and SHO are not present. It appears the entire police station has been vacated since CJP members arrived. Anyway, we have submitted the letter."In its communication, CJP claimed that over 55,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across Delhi over the past three days, disrupting normal life.It alleged arbitrary detentions, physical aggression and prolonged custody involving common people and journalists, besides flagging financial losses suffered by businesses forced to down shutters.The party blamed road closures, barricades and the refusal to allot Jantar Mantar as a protest site for growing public distress. It demanded a scaling down of security deployment, an end to alleged illegal detentions and harassment of independent journalists, and permission to protest at a designated site.Das said, "Protesting peacefully is our democratic right. What happened in the past day (was akin to govt) waging a war against its own citizens."The party said that students, youth and other citizens cannot be prevented from exercising their constitutional right to assemble and protest peacefully.Soon after Jantar Mantar's denotification was announced, Ranka posted on social media, "Why not declare Mt Everest as the designated protest site? Thirty minutes after we went to Delhi Police asking for a date when we can go to Jantar Mantar, it was denotified."CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke wrote on social media, "Today, Modi denotified Jantar Mantar... Tomorrow, he will denotify democracy itself... Anyway, Jantar Mantar was turned into a war zone... Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!"
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders approached Delhi Police to organize a protest addressing issues with the electoral roll revision. Police announced the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, throwing CJP's plan into uncertainty. CJP demanded a scaling down of security deployment, an end to alleged illegal detentions and harassment of independent journalists.

Article Title: Saudi-Houthi crisis: IndiGo cancels flights to Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah
Article Text:
IndiGo, Akasa Air extend Saudi flight suspensions until October 17 amid security concerns

IndiGo and Akasa Air have extended the suspension of flights to and from Saudi Arabia until October 17, 2026, citing the evolving security situation in the Middle East.IndiGo said flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah would remain cancelled until October 17. In a travel advisory, the airline said it was sharing timely updates through the contact details provided at the time of booking. It added that its support teams were available to assist passengers."Your safety and well-being remain our top priority. We are in constant coordination with the relevant authorities to ensure safe operations," IndiGo said.Akasa Air also extended the suspension of all flights to and from Riyadh and Jeddah until October 17, citing the escalating security situation in the Middle East and the associated risks to safe flight operations.In its October 13 advisory, the airline said affected passengers could opt for a full refund, which would be credited to the original source of payment within seven days, or reschedule their travel at no additional cost. Passengers who booked through travel partners were advised to contact them directly for assistance."The safety and well-being of our passengers and crew remain our highest priority," Akasa Air said.This comes as one person was killed and 11 others injured in a fresh attack on Riyadh's international airport on Sunday.On Saturday, a strike claimed by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels killed 13 people and injured more than 300.Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an unidentified projectile struck Terminal 4 of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, triggering a fire.Saudi air defences also intercepted a cruise missile near the airport, destroyed a drone in the Eastern Province and intercepted a ballistic missile fired towards Khamis Mushait.Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority confirmed a strike on Dammam airport late Sunday, adding that damage assessments and safety inspections were under way.The escalation has raised concerns over regional aviation, global oil supplies and shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key maritime route linking the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis and planned to speak with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

Article Title: Peaceful protest fundamental to democracy, will review police action against protesters: Kharge
Article Text:
File photo: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge Tuesday said he’ll review Bengaluru police’s handling of anti-SIR protesters who were detained on Monday, when police forcibly removed demonstrators and manhandled journalists covering the action.“The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. It must be respected, protected and never suppressed,” Kharge said in a post on X. “I have issued instructions to the police to ensure that no peaceful demonstration is disrupted,” he added.Late on Monday, chief minister DK Shivakumar, had posted on X asking Bengaluru police commissioner to “look into this and ensure that the right to peaceful protest is protected”.Kharge also appealed to protesters to cooperate with the police and inform authorities in advance to ensure their safety and protect the rights of others. “The police are here to protect your rights, not to stand in the way of your voice,” he said.The announcement comes after dozens of protesters, including students, lawyers, activists, academics and senior citizens, were detained near KR Circle as they sought to march to the chief electoral officer’s office.They were demanding that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls be scrapped and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign.The action also saw photojournalists covering the protest being assaulted and other journalists manhandled. Plainclothes personnel were among those seen acting aggressively towards protesters and journalists.An activist group, My Vote, My Right, said police confiscated placards and began detaining protesters before they could start the march. Its press release said people were pushed, dragged and forcibly taken away in buses. Police personnel were also seen beating young protesters and pulling at the clothes of women protesters, the group said.One photojournalist was beaten by four police personnel, while three other journalists were manhandled, according to the group.A photojournalist who witnessed the police action said an officer asked him to delete footage he had recorded of police assaulting students inside a bus. As journalists continued filming the detention of women protesters, police personnel objected.“One person came and said, delete it,” the photojournalist recounted. He said police personnel subsequently grabbed his phone, pushed him to the ground and threw the phone aside. Another officer pulled him by the collar, while personnel pushed him from behind and hit him on the leg. An officer also threatened to put him in jail.The incident had drawn criticism on social media, including from Arpita Das, associate professor of writing at Ashoka University, who said her daughter and a friend had been detained after joining the protest. She questioned why this was happening in a Congress-ruled state when young people were supporting the party’s position on SIR. Shivakumar’s X post was in response to Das’ post.The detentions in Bengaluru, incidentally happened on a day both Shivakumar and Kharge were protesting against SIR and police action against demonstrators in Delhi.On Monday, DCP (Central) Akshay M Hakay had said protesters had assembled near KR Circle without permission or prior intimation, contrary to high court directions that demonstrations be held at designated places. Police initially asked them to move to Freedom Park, but they did not comply and were taken into preventive custody before being released, he said.Hakay said police had acted with restraint and sensitivity. Acknowledging friction between police personnel and journalists, he described it as “completely unintentional” and said it had occurred in “straining circumstances”.Kharge Tuesday said: “Our responsibility is not merely to maintain law and order, but to create an environment where every citizen can express dissent freely, peacefully and without fear… In a democracy, peaceful dissent is not a threat to law and order. It is a right that law and order must protect,” he said.
Article Summary: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge Tuesday said he’ll review Bengaluru police’s handling of anti-SIR protesters. Police forcibly removed demonstrators and manhandled journalists covering the action. Protesters were demanding that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls be scrapped.

NEW DELHI: Congress neta Rahul Gandhi Monday told CEC Gyanesh Kumar that he could be forgiven for making a “mistake” if he resigned, telling him that the opposition is after the bigger powers behind him.Addressing a news conf­erence, Rahul said, “Resign, turn approver. Article Title: ICMR sets up high-altitude research centre in Keylong to study health risks in Himalayas
Article Text:
JP Nadda said the centre would help build a strong institutional foundation for research into the health challenges faced by people in the Himalayan region and personnel deployed in high-altitude areas.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From how soldiers acclimatise to thin air at extreme altitudes to how low oxygen levels and harsh winters affect the health of Himalayan communities, a new research centre in Himachal Pradesh will study the distinctive medical challenges of living and working in the mountains.Union health minister Jagat Prakash Nadda on Monday performed the bhumi pujan and laid the foundation stone of the Indian Council of Medical Research's (ICMR) Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research at Keylong, Himachal Pradesh.Built on an ICMR field station established at Keylong nearly a decade ago, the centre will function as a permanent, year-round institution with specialised personnel and state-of-the-art laboratories. It will generate evidence on the health effects of low oxygen levels, extreme cold and changing climatic conditions, with research spanning both military personnel and civilian populations.The research will focus on altitude-related health risks, acclimatisation, maternal and newborn health, child nutrition and disease patterns in Himalayan communities. It will also explore drone-based medicine delivery, digital health and artificial intelligence to improve healthcare access in remote areas.ICMR will combine its research expertise with AFMS’s field experience, with AIIMS Bilaspur studying the effects of high-altitude conditions on patients visiting the region.Nadda said the centre would help build a strong institutional foundation for research into the health challenges faced by people in the Himalayan region and personnel deployed in high-altitude areas. He stressed the need for systematic studies to identify risks and develop appropriate preventive healthcare interventions.Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja, Director General of the Armed Forces Medical Services, said the research would help develop protocols for acclimatisation, early detection and treatment of altitude-related illnesses. ICMR director general Rajiv Bahl said the centre would involve local communities in research aimed at improving health. The findings are expected to benefit Himalayan and border regions. Defence minister of state Sanjay Seth, Jai Ram Thakur and Kangana Ranaut attended the event. Nadda also inaugurated a student science exhibition and launched the centre’s website and video, besides releasing a commemorative postal cover.
Article Summary: The research will focus on altitude-related health risks, acclimatisation, maternal and newborn health, child nutrition and disease patterns. It will also explore drone-based medicine delivery, digital health and artificial intelligence to improve healthcare access in remote areas. The findings are expected to benefit Himalayan and border regions.

Article Title: 'Advance injustice': Allahabad HC flags POCSO Act's rigid application in minor couple cases
Article Text:
The Allahabad high court has urged the law commission to recommend amendments to the POCSO Act.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Allahabad high court has called on the law commission to consider recommending changes to the protection of children from sexual offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, to address cases involving minor couples while taking India's prevailing social realities into account.A two-judge bench comprising justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev said that the strict enforcement of the legislation could, in certain exceptional circumstances, lead to outcomes that “advance injustice rather than justice”, especially when a relationship has resulted in the birth of a child.The comment was made during the court's consideration of Rakesh Yadav's habeas corpus petition, which sought an order to produce his wife.The bench observed that the law appeared not to have adequately considered India's social conditions, where a substantial section of the population remains illiterate or semi-literate and may have limited awareness of their legal and constitutional rights, along with the responsibilities and consequences associated with them.The girl's father told the court that she had studied up to class 5 but could not read a newspaper and was able only to sign her name.He said he had never attended school.The court allowed the man's habeas corpus petition. The couple had eloped, and the girl subsequently gave birth to their child, following which a case was registered against him under the POCSO Act.Court calls for flexibility in exceptional cases"It is definitely not an excuse to be ignorant of the law. The bench noted that the POCSO Act's execution may, in some factual circumstances, lead to outcomes that seem to promote injustice rather than justice if this concept is implemented in a purely pedantic manner."According to the news agency PTI, the court suggested that the law commission consider amendments allowing special judges greater flexibility in exceptional cases to take the specific circumstances into account while deciding an appropriate sentence.It also recommended examining alternative penalties, including community service, in situations where applying the POCSO Act could lead to the unnecessary disruption of a family formed amid a lack of awareness of the law.The bench observed that the existing legislation appeared to have insufficiently considered India's prevailing social realities.Describing the matter as a conflict between human development and the strict application of the law, the court noted that adolescents around the age of 15 may develop emotional and physical maturity that can lead to attraction towards another person.However, the bench stressed that the state must ensure minors continue their education until they reach the age of majority. It also underlined the need to provide them with adequate opportunities to acquire vocational skills and become self-reliant.According to the case records, the couple had eloped and signed an affidavit on September 1, 2025, declaring themselves husband and wife.The state government and the girl's father stated that her date of birth was July 25, 2010.After being separated from her husband, the girl was placed in a Balika Griha, where she subsequently gave birth to a child.The court noted that the case records did not contain a date-of-birth certificate issued by a school or a birth certificate from a municipal authority or panchayat.
Article Summary: The Allahabad high court has called on the law commission to consider recommending changes to the POCSO Act, 2012. A two-judge bench said that the strict enforcement of the legislation could, in certain exceptional circumstances, lead to outcomes that “advance injustice rather than justice” The comment was made during the court's consideration of Rakesh Yadav's habeas corpus petition.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Instead, they are contesting the bypolls as a separate front.Candidates of the main opposition DMK, the AIADMK and the Tamil nationalist Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are also in the fray.The Vanniyar-dominated PMK, which has considerable influence in several northern parts of the state, has not extended support to any party.A key opposition campaign plank is that the bypolls were not a natural outcome but were forced on voters after the TVK “lured AIADMK MLAs” to strengthen its numbers in the Assembly.AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami has already begun campaigning, seeking “justice” over what he has described as the betrayal.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK. He claimed that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position. Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, will be held on October 6.

Article Title: 'Mar gaya,mar gaya tera bhai': 'Punched in chest', how row over metro seat turned deadly in Delhi
Article Text:
Deepak alleged that his brother had been punched in the chest during the altercation.

Mar gaya, mar gaya tera bhai gir gaya

Row over seats reserved for senior citizens

‘He had already died by the time I reached’

Family loses sole breadwinner

Father-son duo arrested





NEW DELHI: “” (He is dead, your brother has fallen down). These were the words Durga Sharma kept repeating over the phone to her younger son, Deepak (45), after his elder brother, Pawan Sharma, became unconscious following an altercation with a father-son duo over seats reserved for senior citizens on a Delhi Metro train on Oct 8.Pawan’s family had been planning to celebrate his 49th birthday on Nov 2, with Deepak preparing a surprise for his elder brother. Instead, the family is now grappling with his death, which Deepak alleges followed an argument with the two men.On Oct 8, Pawan and his mother, Durga (65), were returning to their Yamuna Vihar home after visiting Deepak, who was unwell, in Gurgaon.Sanjay Pratap Singh, a retired IAS officer, and his son, Sidharth Singh, both residents of Noida, boarded the train at Mandi House. According to police, an argument broke out over the seats where Pawan and his mother were sitting.According to Durga, the two rudely asked them to vacate their seats. “We got up, and my son told them they could now lie down on the seats. The older man grabbed Pawan by the collar and slapped him. When he objected, the man’s son assaulted him. When I tried to intervene, the older man restrained me,” she said.Deepak said his brother had already given up the seat but was still subjected to rude remarks.“My brother had given up the seat but was still subjected to rude remarks by the other party.”When the train reached Supreme Court metro station around 5.47 pm, Pawan became unconscious, police said. He was rushed to LNJP Hospital, where he was declared dead.Deepak said he called his mother back after hearing her distressed voice on the phone. She told him she was taking Pawan to hospital in an ambulance. He then spoke to the ambulance staff, who asked him to reach the hospital.Pawan was no more by the time Deepak arrived. “My mother was fainting. The hospital staff did not tell her, but when I reached there, I was told that he had already died,” he said.Deepak alleged that his brother had been punched in the chest during the altercation. “Pawan was not an aggressive person. He was a family man and never fought with anyone.”Pawan’s death has left his wife and two children without their primary financial support. His 19-year-old son is in the first year of college, while his 15-year-old daughter studies in Class X. Pawan worked as a clerk and was the sole breadwinner for the family.After their father’s death, Pawan had taken responsibility for the household, becoming the family’s main support. He had hoped to give his children a better future, Deepak said. “But now, everything is over.”Police recorded Durga’s statement and registered a case against the father-son duo under Sections 105 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to culpable homicide not amounting to murder and acts committed with common intention.Both men were arrested based on evidence collected during the investigation and remanded to 14 days of judicial custody.
Article Summary: Pawan Sharma became unconscious following an altercation with a father-son duo over seats reserved for senior citizens on a Delhi Metro train on Oct 8. Pawan’s family had been planning to celebrate his 49th birthday on Nov 2, with Deepak preparing a surprise for his elder brother. According to police, an argument broke out over seats where Pawan and his mother were sitting.

Article Title: 'They have too much to lose': Trump dismisses claims China, Russia are helping Iran 'at all'
Article Text:
Trump criticised those making the allegations against Beijing and Moscow.

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday dismissed claims that China and Russia were helping Iran, saying he did not believe the two countries were providing assistance to Tehran.In a post on Truth Social, Trump criticised those making the allegations saying he did not believe that Beijing and Moscow were helping Iran "at all," adding that they had "too much to lose"."I see so many comments from the Radical Left Morons and Lunatics that China and Russia are helping the ‘wonderful’ Islamic Republic of Iran," Trump said."If they are, it’s at a very low level, but I don’t believe they are at all. They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast! Thank you for your attention to this matter," he added.Trump has previously described Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin as "neutral" in the conflict.Moscow and Beijing maintain close ties with Tehran, although both have publicly criticised aspects of the US-led military campaign, Reuters reported.Earlier, Russia has warned that the war could trigger a nuclear arms race in the Middle East, while China has condemned Washington's attacks on Iran as a brazen violation of the country's sovereignty.Last month, Trump warned Xi against providing military support to Iran during the Chinese leader's visit to Washington, according to the US ambassador to China, who said Beijing had assured Washington it would not do so.The warning came amid reports that China had supplied Iran with shoulder-fired air-defence missile launchers and helped Tehran find ways to circumvent sanctions on its oil exports.The United States and Iran have been at war since February 28, when US and Israeli forces launched attacks on Iran. Tehran retaliated with strikes on Israel and Gulf countries hosting US military bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon have since killed thousands of people and displaced millions.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump dismissed claims that China and Russia were helping Iran. He said he did not believe the two countries were providing assistance to Tehran. Trump has previously described Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin as "neutral" in the conflict.

Article Title: Drone attack sinks ship off Bulgaria coast, second strike in a week
Article Text:
A drone assault near the Black Sea coast of Bulgaria led to one ship's sinking and damage to another.​

A drone attack sank a ship off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast on Tuesday, while another vessel was also hit, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.According to Reuters, the Maltese-flagged vessel Chelsea 3, which is owned by a Ukrainian company, was struck by three drones about 18 nautical miles off Bulgaria’s coast. All 15 crew members aboard the ship were rescued, while the second vessel sank in the attack.Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said there was no clear evidence identifying those responsible for the attacks, describing the incident as the second of its kind in a week.“This is absolutely unacceptable — another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters,” Radev said, adding that he would speak with Nato secretary-general Mark Rutte.In an earlier incident on October 6, drones struck two merchant ships in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea.The Togo-flagged cargo ship Alfa Watan sank, while the vessel Able, which was carrying grain, was damaged. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for that attack.Russia denied involvement in the attack, with its embassy in Sofia saying the merchant vessel Alfa Watan was not among the targets hit by Russian drones.The Russian defence ministry said the origin of the drones would need to be established through an investigation.The attacks have raised concerns over the security of commercial vessels operating near Bulgaria, a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (Nato).The Black Sea remains a crucial route for grain and other commodities, particularly for Ukraine, and repeated strikes on merchant ships could disrupt maritime trade and increase risks for shipping operators.
Article Summary: Maltese-flagged vessel Chelsea 3, owned by a Ukrainian company, was struck by three drones about 18 nautical miles off Bulgaria’s coast. All 15 crew members aboard the ship were rescued, while the second vessel sank in the attack.

Article Title: South Korea supermarket stabbing leaves 8 injured, suspect arrested
Article Text:
Firefighters and policemen gather outside the scene where several people were injured in a stabbing incident, in Incheon, South Korea (Reuters)

A South Korean supermarket turned into a stabbing scene on Tuesday after a man allegedly went on a knife attack in Incheon, injuring eight people, with a woman in her 20s suffering cardiac arrest.A man allegedly went on a stabbing spree across multiple floors of a supermarket in South Korea’s Incheon on Tuesday, injuring eight people, including a woman in her 20s who suffered cardiac arrest, Reuters reported, citing local media reports.The incident took place in Incheon, west of Seoul, with South Korean media reporting that the suspect was arrested after the attack.A witness told Yonhap News Agency that the man appeared to have knives attached to both hands and moved across several floors of the shopping complex, attacking people before bystanders managed to subdue him.ALSO READ: Qatar Airways, travel portal ordered to pay Rs 3L after denying patient a ticket refund The suspect was identified as a man in his 60s who was wearing an electronic monitoring ankle bracelet at the time of the attack.Authorities are investigating the incident, but the motive behind the stabbing and the circumstances that led to the violence have not yet been established publicly.
Article Summary: A man allegedly went on a stabbing spree across multiple floors of a supermarket in South Korea’s Incheon. Eight people were injured, including a woman in her 20s who suffered cardiac arrest. The suspect was identified as a man in his 60s who was wearing an electronic monitoring bracelet at the time of the attack.
