Article Title: UP shocker: Woman jumps to death after throwing 14-month-old daughter from 2nd floor; child survives
Article Text:
A 20-year-old woman named Roshni died after jumping from her house during her anniversary celebrations (Picture credits: X)





KANPUR: A 20-year-old woman died after allegedly jumping from the second floor of her house in Mardanpur following a family dispute during celebrations marking her third wedding anniversary. Her 14-month-old daughter, whom she allegedly threw from the building moments earlier, survived after being caught by her husband.The woman, Roshni, had been admitted to Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital in critical condition and died on Sunday morning after two days of treatment.Roshni’s husband, Noor Alam, a tailor, celebrated their wedding anniversary on Oct 7 with family members. Later that night, Noor Alam and Ishrat argued over an unspecified issue. Roshni then went to the second floor with her daughter.Family members alleged that Roshni first threw her daughter from the second floor. Noor Alam, who was standing below, caught the child in his arms. Before he could comprehend what had happened, Roshni jumped from the building.Family members took both to a private hospital, where the child was declared out of danger. After primary treatment, Roshni was referred to LLR Hospital on Oct 9.Gujaini SHO Rajan Sharma said they have not received any written complaint from the family yet. Further action would be taken on the basis on autopsy report, he added.
Article Summary: 20-year-old woman named Roshni died after jumping from her house during her anniversary celebrations. Her 14-month-old daughter, whom she allegedly threw from the building moments earlier, survived after being caught by her husband. The woman had been admitted to Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital in critical condition and died on Sunday morning.

Article Title: How janta got protest mantra. And lost it
Article Text:
Jantar Mantar has historically served as a significant venue for protests in central Delhi





NEW DELHI: For decades, Jantar Mantar has been more than a stretch of road where people gather with placards, raise slogans and sit on dharna.For many, it has been the place where a grievance that went unheard elsewhere could find an audience from national television cameras and newspaper reporters to the very people protesters wanted to hold accountable.That familiar address for dissent, however, has now lost its designated status as a protest venue after being de-notified by Delhi Police The change is not merely about shifting crowds from one location to another, but raises a larger question about what happens when a protest loses the visibility that came with its location.Anupam, who has led several protests at Jantar Mantar for youth causes and is now associated with Congress, said the recent protest was about more than the issue concerning CEC Gyanesh Kumar.Protesters were asserting their right to demonstrate, but many were detained before they could reach the venue, he added.“Jantar Mantar Road is located in the heart of central Delhi, roughly 1.5km from Parliament House and very close to major ministries, govt headquarters and CP,” he said.For protesters, that location meant being close to the institutions they sought to question. It also placed their demands within easy reach of newsrooms.Journalists and camera crews could reach the site quickly, giving even relatively small demonstrations a chance to attract attention that a larger gathering on the outskirts might struggle to secure.But Jantar Mantar’s significance was not confined to movements with national leaders, large banners or organisational backing.Sidharth Mishra, author of Delhi Political, said the venue also provided space to people whose problems rarely attracted attention.Large organisations and well-known campaigners, he said, could find other ways to amplify their voices, including through social media. Smaller groups and individuals don’t necessarily have those options.“They were people whose voices were not heard in their states, those affected by bureaucracy or cheated by banks and cooperatives. Many times, their stories would catch a reporter’s attention and their problems would get resolved,” Mishra said.He questioned whether such protesters would be able to afford the alternatives: “Do they have so much money to book Ramlila or other grounds?”The history of protest venues in the capital offers a glimpse of how Jantar Mantar acquired this role. For decades after Independence, the Boat Club lawns near India Gate were a major gathering point, bringing protesters close to Parliament and govt’s principal offices. Mahendra Singh Tikait’s massive farmers’ mobilisation in 1988 became one of the defining episodes in the debate over large demonstrations in central Delhi.As concerns over security, traffic and public order prompted tighter restrictions around prominent central spaces, protesters moved to other locations. In the early 1990s, tents and demonstrations along the stretch now known as Kartavya Path were dismantled, and Jantar Mantar emerged as a prominent alternative.Among the first protest held here was a major mobilisation in 1993, led by then DUSU president Ashish Sood along with 33 civil organisations, that brought thousands of students to the venue for a “Jail Bharo” campaign against Centre’s anti-student measures and economic policies.Over the years, the road became associated with causes that extended beyond student politics. Anna Hazare ’s 2011 anti-corruption movement demanding Jan Lokpal Bill drew thousands. In 2015, military veterans held hunger strikes for One Rank, One Pension’s implementation.TN farmers staged a 41-day protest in 2017 to highlight agrarian distress, while prominent wrestlers chose the venue in 2023 to raise demands for action over allegations of sexual harassment against former WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh Jantar Mantar’s place in history has not been uninterrupted. In Oct 2017, NGT prohibited protests and loudspeakers amid complaints of noise, but SC restored the right to protest in July 2018.
Article Summary: Jantar Mantar has historically served as a significant venue for protests in central Delhi. It has now lost its designated status as a protest venue after being de-notified by Delhi Police. The change raises a larger question about what happens when a protest loses the visibility that came with its location.

Article Title: Kochi crash that killed 3: Video of mother gifting Mini Cooper to 19-year-old surfaces
Article Text:
Suhail was gifted luxury car by mother on his birthday

Teen driver, three others arrested





KOCHI: A video showing a mother gifting her 19-year-old son, Suhail Sajeev, a Mini Cooper has surfaced after the luxury car allegedly rammed a scooter in Kerala’s Nedumbassery, killing three young people.Police said Suhail’s mother had gifted him the car for his birthday. The video has surfaced amid an investigation into the crash, which took place on Airport Road around 1.45am on Sunday.The Mini Cooper allegedly rammed the scooter from behind, killing all three people riding the two-wheeler. The victims were identified as Devika (21), Gopika (22) and Iyas (21).The video of the birthday gift comes to light alongside other clips purportedly showing Suhail driving at high speeds. An earlier Instagram video showed the car’s speedometer climbing from 204kmph to 220kmph.Suhail was arrested on charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Police suspect he was driving under the influence of alcohol, though forensic reports were awaited.His three co-passengers have also been arrested, with police alleging they allowed him to drive despite knowing he was intoxicated.The Excise Department has initiated action against three bars suspected of serving alcohol to the group, as Suhail is below Kerala’s legal drinking age of 23.Police are examining CCTV footage, witness accounts and other evidence to establish the circumstances of the crash.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Teen driver, three others arrested after Mini Cooper allegedly rammed a scooter, killing three young people. Suhail Sajeev's mother gifted him the car for his birthday. Police suspect he was driving under the influence of alcohol, though forensic reports were awaited.

Article Title: Beer spilled on woman, man beaten to death by bouncers at Delhi nightclub
Article Text:
Eyewitness recounts Delhi nightclub assault that killed Daljeet





NEW DELHI: A 29-year-old man was allegedly beaten to death by bouncers and staff at a nightclub in northwest Delhi following a dispute after one of his friends allegedly spilled beer on a woman.According to polce the incident took place late on Saturday at a nightclub in the area under Sarai Rohilla police station.The deceased, Daljeet, a resident of Raghuvir Nagar, is survived by his wife, eight-year-old son and father. Police have arrested some people in connection with the case and are making efforts to identify and apprehend the other accused.According to news agency PTI, Daljeet had gone to the nightclub with some friends when one of them spilled beer on a woman, triggering an argument. The club's bouncers allegedly assaulted Daljeet and his friends. The attack continued despite the group apologising.The situation escalated when waiters at the club allegedly joined the assault, beating Daljeet and his friends with sticks and glass bottles. When they tried to escape, the attackers allegedly dragged them back inside and assaulted them again. Daljeet sustained the most serious injuries.His friends took him to his residence in Raghuvir Nagar, where he collapsed near the entrance. He was then rushed to Guru Gobind Singh Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.Police have seized the nightclub's CCTV digital video recorder and are examining the footage to establish the sequence of events and identify those involved.
Article Summary: Daljeet, 29, was allegedly beaten to death by bouncers and staff at a nightclub in northwest Delhi following a dispute after one of his friends spilled beer on a woman. Police have arrested some people in connection with the case and are making efforts to identify and apprehend the other accused.

Article Title: Chose dark, CCTV-free cellar: How ex-guard planned 5-year-old’s murder for quick money
Article Text:
After allegedly committing the murder, Vikram walked out of the gated community through the main gate and called the girl’s family to demand a ransom.





HYDERABAD: Over 24 hours after the ghastly murder of a five-year-old girl at Villa Orchids in Kowkoor, Bollaram police arrested the prime accused Vikram Kumar , a former security guard of the housing society late on Sunday night.Cops said that the accused spent less than 25 minutes inside the gated community to carry out the crime, deliberately choosing a secluded, dark spot in the clubhouse cellar with no CCTV coverage.“Vikram confessed to have killed the girl to make quick money. He made her his target as he knew she stepped out to play in the evenings and that her family, which maintained a low profile, could afford to pay a ransom,” Malkajgiri police commissioner, B Sumathi, said while announcing his arrest.A native of Nalanda in Bihar, Vikram had joined the society’s security staff four months ago. He was fired just a day before the crime for poor conduct.Police said that the accused kept an eye on the girl, who had gone into the clubhouse to watch Bathukamma celebrations, and allegedly lured her to the under-construction cellar within the property, soon after she stepped out -- under some unknown pretext. Since the minor was acquainted to Vikram, she didn’t hesitate to follow him.Once in the cellar, he allegedly used construction material lying around to strangle her to death. He then tied her hands and legs, fastened bricks to her body and drowned her in a water sump, the commissioner added.Immediately afterwards, Vikram exited the gated community through the main gate and called the minor’s family to demand a ransom. He had retrieved their numbers from the register kept at the society’s main gate.While both the child’s father and grandfather, who the accused spoke to, agreed to pay the ransom of Rs 20 lakh on condition that Vikram first make a WhatsApp video call to prove that the girl was alive, he refused to do so.They family lodged a police complaint at around 9.45 pm on Saturday.“For the first four hours after receiving the complaint, we checked footage from 130 CCTV cameras to locate the minor girl. Simultaneously searches were also conducted at Secunderabad railway station and other places to trace the accused, based on his mobile tower location,” Sumathi said.After reviewing the investigation, at around 2 am on Sunday, police decided to search within the gated community, focusing on secluded parts of the campus. “That is when our team eventually found the girl’s body in the cellar, a spot that residents rarely visited,” she added.Incidentally, residents of the community told police, Vikram had been caught smoking and drinking in the cellar just a few days earlier. When the matter came to the notice of his security agency, he was dismissed from his job.“Meanwhile, after committing the crime, Vikram returned to his room in Kowkoor that he shared with other employees of the security agency. He later travelled using different modes of transport, including an autorickshaw, and reached Patancheru, where he was apprehended from late on Sunday night,” said the police commissioner.After securing his judicial remand, police said they will seek custody of the accused for further interrogation. “We are also waiting for information from Nalanda police to verify Vikram’s antecedents,” Sumathi added.
Article Summary: Vikram Kumar, a former security guard of Villa Orchids in Kowkoor, was arrested late on Sunday night. Vikram confessed to have killed the girl to make quick money, police said. He was fired just a day before the crime for poor conduct. The accused kept an eye on the girl, who had gone into the clubhouse to watch Bathukamma celebrations.

Article Title: Anti-CEC protest in Delhi: Detainees say taken 40km away, beaten
Article Text:
Protesters in New Delhi reported being beaten and detained after a demonstration on Sunday

How detainees were moved from CP to Chhawla to Pandwala Khurd





NEW DELHI: Many protesters detained Sunday said they were beaten and taken to a community centre in Pandwala Khurd, 38km from Rajiv Chowk, at 8pm and left without phones and medical help. They alleged minors were also detained.The claims were confirmed by HC advocate Gaurav Jain, who reached the site. Police denied claims of beatings, and said food, water and first aid were provided. The protesters were released around 9.30pm.Nearly 38km from Rajiv Chowk, Delhi High Court advocate Gaurav Jain, found himself at a community centre in Pandwala Khurd, a village he had never heard of, while responding to an SOS by protesters detained Sunday. They alleged minors had been detained alongside other protesters."The location kept changing from Kapashera to Chhawla to ultimately this village I'd never heard of before," he said.Jain reached around 8pm with other lawyers. He alleged he was stopped by cops and was not allowed to meet detainees for several minutes.He said he then called 112 for the police control room van and also contacted the principal magistrate of juvenile justice board-7, asking her to seek a status report from the SHO on the detained minors.Arjun, a detained protester, said in a video message after release, that he was protesting at Connaught Place around 3pm Sunday. He said he saw the cops dragging a couple crossing the road, with no female officers nearby. "The police jumped on us and detained us when we tried to help. They then called women constables," he said.The protesters said they were first taken to an isolated stretch near Rajiv Chowk."We were told to sit in rows... the cops then asked us to hand over our phones and passwords. An inspector... tried accessing one person's photo gallery, saying he was deleting 'aaj ka video'. When the person protested, he was slapped," Arjun alleged.The protesters were then put on another police bus that was divided into 7-8 compartments using iron rods. Arjun alleged that four minors were among them.Despite assurances that cooperation would ensure proper treatment, he alleged, they were beaten up. "There was no space to run as they kept beating us," he said. The bus reached Chhawla police station around 6.53pm.The protesters were taken to the community centre in Pandwala Khurd, where their details, including those of the minors, were recorded.Police, however, said that claims of violence at Pandwala Khurd were baseless and false. It said that no protester was beaten up or assaulted by personnel at the site."Officers had made arrangements to ensure that those detained or present at the location were provided with basic assistance and did not face unnecessary hardship. They came around 8pm and were allowed to leave around 9.30 pm," a senior police officer said.Jain, however, was caught on video pleading with the CRPF personnel guarding the gate: "IO sahab, hume andar aane dijiye. Humare bulane pe hi police aayi hai."The lawyers eventually entered in the PCR van they had called, Jain said. The protesters were released around 9.30pm. One detainee appeared to have injuries on his hand."They had taken away everyone's phone, and when he resisted, he was beaten up. When I asked whether he had received medical assistance, they took him away in a van to help," Jain stated.Police said food and drinking water were provided to the protesters, while those who had sustained injuries were given first aid. Police also denied allegations that anyone's mobile phone had been snatched or that any protester had been subjected to misbehaviour by personnel deployed at Pandwala Khurd."No woman or any other protester was harassed during the operation. Police arrangements continued even after the protesters were released. Buses were provided to facilitate their movement from Pandwala Khurd to the nearest metro stations and bus stands to access public transport and continue their journeys," the officer said.
Article Summary: Protesters detained Sunday said they were beaten and taken to a community centre in Pandwala Khurd. They alleged minors were also detained. Police denied claims of beatings, and said food, water and first aid were provided. The protesters were released around 9.30pm.

Article Title: ‘Jantar Mantar has been reclaimed’: CJP’s Saurav Das urges youth to continue campaign before fresh detention
Article Text:
Saurav Das, leader of the Cockroach Janta Party, reported that police have detained activists at Jantar Mantar

CJP claims entry to Jantar Mantar despite protest-site status being withdrawn

CJP had given Delhi Police 24-hour ultimatum over protest date





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das on Monday claimed that party members had entered Jantar Mantar despite the venue being removed from Delhi’s list of designated protest sites, and said they were being detained by police.Announcing the development in a post on X, Das declared that the protest site had been “reclaimed” and urged young supporters to continue the campaign.“JANTAR MANTAR HAS BEEN RECLAIMED!WE HAVE ENTERED JANTAR MANTAR AND NOW WE ARE BEING DETAINED!But this is a message to all of us young gen! We can do it! Gyanu, you’re done bro!” Das posted.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke claimed that Das, Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and other party members had been detained. He shared the claim on social media.The claim comes a day after Delhi Police removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest venues, ending its long-standing status as a site for demonstrations in the capital.The decision followed a review of alternative protest locations by a committee constituted by the Union home ministry. Police have designated Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi as alternative venues for protests.Earlier on Monday, CJP activists visited Parliament Street police station and asked Delhi Police to specify a date and time for their proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar, giving the force 24 hours to respond.Das had said the party was willing to let the police choose the date and time, arguing that the authorities could no longer cite the requirement to apply 10 days in advance as a reason for delaying the protest.The CJP has been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Its earlier attempt to hold a demonstration at Jantar Mantar on October 10 was thwarted by a major security operation, during which party leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das claims entry to Jantar Mantar despite venue being removed from Delhi’s list of designated protest sites. Das declared that the protest site had been ‘reclaimed’ and urged young supporters to continue the campaign.

Article Title: ‘Ja nahi rahe the, andar ghus gaye’: Ashutosh Ranka on CJP members’ Jantar Mantar detention
Article Text:
Cockroach Janta Party leader Ashutosh Ranka alleged that members had already entered Jantar Mantar

CJP members jump gate to enter Jantar Mantar

Security tightened in Delhi





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Ashutosh Ranka on Tuesday alleged that party members had entered Jantar Mantar before being detained by Delhi Police, responding to a user on X who said they had been detained while going to the protest site.“सर जा नहीं रहे थे, अंदर घुस गए,” Ranka wrote, roughly translating to, “Sir, they weren’t just going there; they entered inside.”The remark came after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ranka were detained by Delhi Police while attempting to reach Jantar Mantar, police sources said.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke also claimed that several other members, including Ajinkya Shinde, had been detained.In a post on X, Dipke said CJP members carrying the national flag had entered Jantar Mantar before police detained them.“Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police,” Dipke said.He named Ranka, Das, Shinde and other team members as among those detained.“You cannot denotify the resistance,” Dipke added, tagging Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Dipke also shared a video purportedly showing CJP members jumping over a gate to enter Jantar Mantar and raising slogans such as “Bharat Mata ki Jai”.Police personnel are seen rushing towards them and taking them away.The detentions came amid heightened security in the national capital following calls for demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Delhi Police has deployed a large number of personnel across the city to maintain law and order. The CJP has been demanding Kumar’s resignation and action over alleged voter-list irregularities, while authorities have cited security and public-order concerns surrounding the proposed demonstrations.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Ashutosh Ranka on Tuesday alleged that party members had entered Jantar Mantar before being detained by Delhi Police. The remark came after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ranka were detained. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke also claimed that several other members, including Ajinkya Shinde, had been detained. The detentions came amid heightened security in the national capital.

Article Title: Caught on cam: Punjab anti-drug activist shot dead after confronting chemist over alleged drug sales
Article Text:
Facing bullet injury, Parwinder Jhota tried to ran away but fell down at a distance and was declared dead at the hospital.





BATHINDA: Anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh Jhota was shot dead at Mansa on Tuesday morning. Four others sustained injuries when a chemist fired multiple shots at Parwinder.The chemist, identified as Ashwani Kumkar when confronted by Parwinder along with others, fired inside his shop and followed Parwinder Jhota out in the market while openly flaunting a revolver and fired again at Jhota.Parwinder was preparing a video clip while getting online on social networking site Facebook when the chemist fired at him and the firing incident was recorded on camera. When taken to Mansa Civil Hospital, Parwinder (45) was declared brought dead.Parwinder Singh was acting against the drug menace for a long time and lately he was raising voice against certain medical stores accusing them of selling intoxicating pills and synthetic drugs apart from other prohibited substances.ALSO READ: 'Rahul grabbed my hand, pushed me': Pregnant journalist alleges assault during protest On Tuesday morning, Jhota met an old person who had bought synthetic drugs from a medical store. Jhota took the man to the medical store and asked the chemist why he was selling prohibited substances.Over it he had some exchanges and the store owner pulled a weapon and fired at Jhota, who was an active member of anti drug brigade.Facing bullet injury, Parwinder Jhota ran away but the chemist fired at him again and finally Parwinder fell down in another shop.As per information, Jhota in July 2023 had dishounored the same chemist by putting a garland of shoes around his neck accusing him of selling synthetic drugs.Then a case was registered against Jhota and he was arrested. The activists of a number of social and farmer organisations held protests for days for discharging Jhota from the case.Buckling under public pressure, the state government relented and paved the way for the release of Parwinder Singh. Parwinder came out of jail on September 11 after spending nearly two months in jail. His release was ensured after complainant had approached the court for withdrawing the complaint.The chemist is also facing cases for selling prohibited substances.Mansa Civil Hospital SMO Dr Gurmail Singh said that 5 injured were brought to the hospital with one of them identified as Parwinder Singh had three bullets, one in right thigh and one each on either side of the abdomen, who succumbed to injuries while four others identified as Kulwinder Singh, Gobind Singh, Baltej Singh and Happy too sustained injuries.Mansa SSP Vaibhav Chaudhary said the shopkeeper has been identified and police is on the job to arrest him.ALSO READ: Pakistan angle under probe? Delhi Police files 4 FIRs over fake posts since October 10
Article Summary: Anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh Jhota was shot dead at Mansa on Tuesday morning. The chemist, identified as Ashwani Kumkar, fired inside his shop and followed him out in the market while openly flaunting a revolver. Facing bullet injury, Parwinders tried to ran away but fell down at a distance and was declared dead at the hospital.

Article Title: 'Tears in both lungs, shock and haemorrhage': What post-mortem revealed in UP bizman's death; family accuses model Shraddha Dubey of murder
Article Text:
Image Credit: X

Mother accuses girlfriend, others of assault and murder

Police search for people linked to case





LUCKNOW: A post-mortem report of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma, who died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment near Balu Adda on October 9, records 11 entries detailing external injuries and six broad categories of internal findings.The report notes tears in both lungs, injuries to the liver and spleen, substantial internal bleeding and a fracture of the right pelvic bone. Doctors attributed his death to shock and haemorrhage resulting from the injuries.Police are investigating whether Sharma jumped, was pushed or fell accidentally. Investigators are examining CCTV footage, witness statements and physical evidence from the scene to reconstruct the sequence of events.They are also considering a crime scene recreation to establish the likely point of impact and determine whether the evidence at the site is consistent with the injuries recorded in the autopsy. Officials said the post-mortem findings alone do not establish how Sharma went over the edge.Sharma’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, has accused his girlfriend, model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey, a driver, an associate identified as Adil, and others of assaulting and murdering her son.Hazratganj police have registered an FIR based on her complaint. The allegations have not yet been established.Ranjana told police that she received a call from Adil around 7pm on October 9, informing her that Sharma’s condition had worsened and that he was being taken to King George’s Medical University (KGMU).She alleged that when the family reached the hospital, the people who had accompanied Sharma showed him to them from a distance before fleeing. Doctors subsequently declared him dead, according to her complaint.Ranjana also alleged that Dubey had harassed Sharma for months, threatened to implicate him in false cases and damage his reputation, and used blackmail and violence to pressure him into continuing the relationship.Police have yet to establish these allegations.Assistant commissioner of police (Hazratganj) Rajneesh Verma said further action would depend on the evidence gathered during the investigation.Police teams have conducted searches in Rae Bareli and Sitapur to trace people linked to the case, he said.Investigators are continuing to examine the medical findings alongside other evidence to establish the circumstances surrounding Sharma’s death.
Article Summary: Mother accuses girlfriend, others of assault and murder of her son. Shiva Sharma, 28, died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment near Balu Adda on October 9. Post-mortem report notes tears in both lungs, injuries to the liver and internal bleeding.

Article Title: Affair, pistol, 2 bullets: How woman and her lover plotted husband’s murder in Noida
Article Text:
Anshul (L) and Nisha (R)

A relationship that turned into a murder plot

Pistol procured from village, hidden in room

How the shooting allegedly unfolded





GHAZIABAD: A two-year affair, a plan allegedly hatched a week in advance and a country-made pistol were at the centre of a murder in Khoda Colony, where a 30-year-old woman and her lover allegedly conspired to kill her husband so they could marry each other.Police said the accused, Pappu alias Ganga Bhagat, allegedly shot Anshul twice while he was alone at home on Saturday, then fled.Nisha and Pappu, 35, were arrested on Sunday following a tip-off, ACP (Indirapuram) Suryabali Maurya said. Police recovered an illegal .315-bore country-made pistol allegedly used in the crime at Pappu’s instance.The two have been booked for murder under Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and under relevant provisions of the Arms Act.The case came to light after Anshul’s sister approached police in the early hours of Sunday. In her complaint, she alleged that Nisha and Pappu had been in a relationship and wanted to eliminate Anshul so they could marry.Anshul and Nisha had married in 2015 and had two children. They lived in a rented room in Vandana Vihar, Khoda, and both worked at a stitching company in Noida.Pappu, who is the husband of their maternal cousin, had also been living with them, police said.According to Anshul’s sister, he had repeatedly complained about Nisha’s relationship with Pappu. The family had tried to resolve the matter internally, allegedly because of social stigma, but the relationship continued.During questioning, Pappu allegedly told police that he and Nisha had planned the murder around a week before the shooting. He allegedly procured a country-made pistol and cartridges from his village, and the two hid them in the room, the ACP said.Pappu also told police that his first wife had died and his second wife lived in their village.Anshul had taken two days off from work, while Nisha continued going to work, police said. On Saturday, when Anshul was alone at home, Pappu allegedly arrived around 1pm, saying he had come to eat.After the meal, he allegedly took out the pistol and fired two rounds at Anshul before fleeing. Anshul died on the spot, according to police.Pappu later allegedly called Nisha and told her about the killing. The ACP said the two had remained in frequent contact throughout Saturday.Police have registered a case under the relevant provisions of the BNS and the Arms Act.
Article Summary: Nisha and Pappu, 35, were arrested on Sunday following a tip-off. Police recovered an illegal.315-bore country-made pistol allegedly used in the crime. Anshul and Nisha had married in 2015 and had two children. They lived in a rented room in Vandana Vihar, Khoda.

Article Title: ‘We’ll kill you’: How a late-night cab ride turned into a 15-minute ordeal for Mumbai student
Article Text:
An 18-year-old student reported being kidnapped by three men while taking a cab in Mumbai (AI image)





MUMBAI: An 18-year-old first-year university student has accused three men of kidnapping him in an aggregator cab, driving him around Juhu for 15 minutes, threatening him with a knife and extorting Rs 14,250 before he was let go early on Oct 10.Juhu police registered a case of kidnapping, extortion and robbery against history-sheeters Azad Maniyar (34), Dipesh Chavan (29) and Mondaya Devendra alias Kishan (30) who allegedly forced PA Agarwal into the cab, stole Rs 5,250 from his pocket and compelled him to transfer Rs 9,000 through an e-wallet. They allegedly made Agarwal call his sister before transferring money through UPI.Police caught the three accused at their hideouts in Andheri within 12 hours of the incident involving Agarwal at 1.30 am on Oct 10. “The accused allegedly forced Agarwal into a cab he had booked to return to his PG accommodation, assaulted the driver, forced him inside and sped away. The trio were tracked through technical analysis using the phone number through which money was credited from Agarwal’s account to an e-wallet. Agarwal had earlier gone to drop his aunt’s daughter and her three friends after they had dinner on Oct 9,” said a police officer of the Juhu police station.According to Agarwal’s complaint, three unidentified men allegedly assaulted an Uber driver and forced Agarwal to remain in the car after he dropped his aunt’s daughter and her three friends at a girls’ hostel in Vile Parle (West) around 1.30 am. Agarwal said one man opened the driver’s door, slapped him and questioned where the passengers had come from. The man allegedly told Agarwal there had been a rape at a girls’ hostel in Yenda the previous day and claimed they were union members. Agarwal, who said he was frightened, remained in the car. One of the men, identified by a companion as Azad, allegedly instructed the Uber driver where to drive and took Agarwal around Juhu and other areas. His two companions followed the car on a scooter, the FIR said.Police said Maniyar allegedly threatened Agarwal with a knife near Juhu Ruia Park and forced him to transfer Rs 5,000 to a UPI account. Two accomplices, who had followed them on a scooter, allegedly restrained Agarwal while Maniyar took Rs 5,250 from his trouser pocket. “The group later allegedly forced Agarwal to obtain money from his sister and transfer another Rs 4,000 to the same account. They allegedly threatened to kill him if he disclosed the incident before releasing him near Mithibai College. Agarwal contacted friends and went to lodge a complaint. At the police station, he identified a man detained by patrolling personnel after a fight on VM Road,” said the police.
Article Summary: 18-year-old student reported being kidnapped by three men while taking a cab in Mumbai. Azad Maniyar (34), Dipesh Chavan (29) and Mondaya Devendra alias Kishan (30) allegedly forced him to transfer Rs 9,000 through an e-wallet. Police caught the three accused at their hideouts in Andheri within 12 hours.

Article Title: ‘I have not been transferred’: Tukaram Mundhe denies rumours, vows to continue Maharashtra FDA crackdown
Article Text:
Tukaram Mundhe, the Maharashtra FDA Commissioner, has denied rumors of his transfer from the organization

Tukaram Mundhe’s FDA crackdown draws public attention

Mundhe appointed secretary of MPSC paper leak inquiry panel





MUMBAI: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) commissioner Tukaram Mundhe on Monday denied speculation about his transfer, saying he continues to head the department and its enforcement drive against unsafe food, adulterated products and substandard medicines will go on.The clarification came amid buzz about a possible transfer of the senior IAS officer, who has seen frequent transfers during his administrative career.The speculation gained traction after the state government named Mundhe secretary of a five-member committee set up to probe alleged paper leaks and irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) examinations."No, I have not been transferred from FDA," Mundhe said in a post on X on Monday night."I continue to serve as Commissioner, FDA Maharashtra. Our fight against unsafe, substandard, adulterated food and spurious, substandard drugs goes on," he added.Mundhe’s tenure as FDA commissioner has attracted considerable attention, with consumers welcoming the department’s intensified action against food safety violations, even as sections of the restaurant and food business industry have opposed measures taken against their establishments.The FDA has stepped up inspections, raids and enforcement action against eateries and food businesses over alleged violations, including the sale or use of unsafe and adulterated products.It has also acted against establishments over licensing and compliance issues as part of its effort to enforce food safety regulations.While consumers have appreciated the emphasis on accountability and food safety, some restaurant operators have resisted the action. Certain enforcement measures have also been challenged in courts, bringing aspects of the FDA’s regulatory drive under legal scrutiny.The enforcement campaign has kept Mundhe’s tenure in the spotlight, with food safety compliance and the functioning of eateries receiving greater public attention.Mundhe’s appointment to the committee probing alleged paper leaks in MPSC examinations followed protests over the functioning of the state recruitment body.Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said last week that the five-member committee would examine the tenures of current and former chairpersons and members of the MPSC.The panel has been tasked with investigating allegations of paper leaks and irregularities in examinations conducted by the commission.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Tukaram Mundhe has denied rumors of his transfer from the organization. The clarification came amid buzz about a possible transfer of the senior IAS officer. The speculation gained traction after the state government named Mundhe secretary of a five-member committee set up to probe alleged paper leaks and irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission examinations.

Article Title: 'Ukraine has not attacked Russian oil refineries for 2 days': Zelenskyy on Trump's 'energy ceasefire'
Article Text:
Zelenskyy calls Russia sanctions relief without de-escalation deal ‘obvious weakness’

Also Read |

Russia on Trump's 'energy ceasefire'

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Ukraine retaliate if Russia continues its attacks on energy infrastructure? Yes, they have the right to defend themselves No, they should pursue diplomatic avenues 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday that Kyiv has not attacked Russian oil refineries for two days following US President Donald Trump’s declaration of an “energy ceasefire” between Ukraine and Russia.However, Zelenskyy accused Moscow of continuing to target Ukraine’s energy facilities and critical infrastructure despite the "ceasefire."“Ukraine has not carried out strikes on Russian oil refineries or the energy sector in general for the two days since the American President announced an energy ceasefire. But Russia did not heed the American President. During this time, the Russians have attacked both our energy facilities and our critical infrastructure,” Zelenskyy wrote on X.He described Russia’s continued attacks as “clear signals” that the Kremlin had no intention of halting strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. However, he reiterated that Kyiv remained committed to de-escalation through reciprocal measures.“Nineteen regions of our country have come under attack in these two days alone. Our position remains unchanged: Ukraine is ready for reciprocal steps toward de-escalation, and effective pressure on Russia is needed to make de-escalation happen.Wars end when the aggressor realizes that it cannot prolong the war,” Zelenskyy added.His remarks came two days after US President Donald Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate “energy ceasefire” in the war, which began on February 24, 2022.“Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform.In response, Zelenskyy said the announcement was “news to me” but added that Kyiv was ready to abide by the ceasefire provided Moscow did the same.Reciprocal attacks on energy infrastructure have become a central point in the Ukraine-Russia conflict.Meanwhile, the Kremlin confirmed on Tuesday that discussions on an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine were ongoing but declined to provide further details.Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov did not clarify with whom Moscow was holding talks on the proposed ceasefire.Russia’s defence ministry, meanwhile, rejected Zelenskyy’s allegation that Russian forces had targeted Ukrainian energy facilities in overnight attacks.
Article Summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday that Kyiv has not attacked Russian oil refineries for two days. However, he accused Moscow of continuing to target Ukraine’s energy facilities and critical infrastructure. His remarks came two days after US President Donald Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate “energy ceasefire”

Article Title: Gym trainer accused of repeatedly raping 23-year-old, making obscene videos of 80 women
Article Text:
A 22-year-old gym trainer, Arif Shaikh, has been taken into custody following grave accusations from a 23-year-old woman

Case over objectionable remarks during Navratri





NALASOPARA: A 22-year-old gym trainer and social media influencer has been arrested by Nalasopara police after a 23-year-old woman accused him of repeatedly raping her on the pretext of marriage.The complainant has also alleged that he lured 70 to 80 women into relationships, recorded obscene videos of them and sold the footage on pornographic websites. Police said they were investigating the allegations and verifying the claims.The accused, identified as Arif Shaikh, was arrested late Monday night after the woman approached the police. His mother, Ruksana, and cousin Sahil Shaikh have also been named in the case.According to the complaint, the woman met Arif on social media last year. She alleged that he promised to marry her and subsequently pressured her to live with him. During this period, he allegedly forced her to have sexual relations with him repeatedly.The complainant further alleged that Arif and his mother pressured her to convert her religion and assaulted her. She also accused Arif's cousin, Sahil, of attempting to sexually assault her.The woman claimed that she later found videos on Arif's mobile phone showing him engaging in sexual acts with several women. She subsequently approached local Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) functionaries for assistance and lodged a complaint with Nalasopara police on Monday night.According to the complainant, Arif used Instagram to target Hindu women, establish relationships with them and record intimate videos without their knowledge or consent.She alleged that he had trapped at least 70 to 80 women in a similar manner and sold their videos on pornographic websites. Police are examining the videos allegedly recovered from his mobile phone and investigating whether other women were also targeted.Local MNS leaders have demanded a thorough investigation into the allegations. Sanjeev Mehra, a local MNS functionary, said the matter needed to be investigated in detail, particularly in view of the alleged videos involving several women."We have received a complaint from one woman and registered a case accordingly. Some obscene videos of women have been found on the mobile phone, and we are investigating the matter from that angle," said Vishal Valvi, senior police inspector at Nalasopara police station. He added that the allegations made by the complainant were being verified.Police have registered a case against Arif, his mother and his cousin under relevant provisions relating to rape, wrongful confinement, assault and other offences. Further investigation is underway.In a separate case, Nalasopara police registered an offence against Arif on Sunday over alleged objectionable remarks about Hindu women during Navratri celebrations.According to a complaint filed by Shiv Upadhyay of the Sakal Hindu organisation, Arif allegedly made controversial remarks about the sale of condoms at gyms during Navratri and claimed that he could lure 30 to 40 women. A video of the alleged remarks was reportedly recorded by one of his friends.Based on the complaint, police registered a case against Arif under relevant provisions relating to the alleged promotion of religious enmity and the Information Technology Act.Police said the two cases were being investigated separately.
Article Summary: A 23-year-old woman has accused gym trainer Arif Shaikh of repeatedly raping her on the pretext of marriage. She has also alleged that he lured 70 to 80 women into relationships, recorded obscene videos of them and sold the footage on pornographic websites. Police have arrested Arif and his mother, Ruksana, and cousin Sahil Shaikh.

Article Title: Nuclear sites fortified, loyalists rallied: Iran braces for possible US attacks after midterms
Article Text:
File photo: Iranian missiles are displayed next to a banner with a picture of Iran's Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, on a street in Tehran, Iran

Iran threatens US personnel, shipping

Iran has strengthened defences around sensitive nuclear sites and stepped up efforts to rally domestic support as it prepares for possible renewed US strikes after the November 3 midterm elections, the Wall Street Journal reported. Tehran has also warned regional officials that a fresh conflict could spill across the Gulf, with threats of land incursions into neighbouring countries and attacks on regional infrastructure, US forces and commercial shipping.The warnings, conveyed by Iranian officials in public statements and private conversations with regional counterparts, are part of Tehran’s effort to deter potential American attacks after the November 3 midterm elections.Some Iranian officials have hinted that Iranian forces could cross into neighbouring countries if Washington resumes strikes, people familiar with the warnings told the WSJ.Iran’s top national security official, Mohsen Rezaei, said on Sunday that Tehran could target the United Arab Emirates, as well as data centres and internet cables across the region.Tehran has separately warned Arab officials that it could strike regional targets, including Saudi oil facilities, if hostilities resume, according to people familiar with the discussions.Such threats would add to the security concerns facing Saudi Arabia, which has also come under attack from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels.Washington and Tehran have been in a prolonged military stand-off but Iran has steadily been rebuilding its capacity for further fighting rather than making concessions. Iran has limited ability to defend itself against advanced American fighter jets, high-altitude bombers and cruise missiles, giving it an incentive to threaten a broader regional conflict to raise the potential costs of a US attack.Iran has also warned mediators that it could more aggressively target American personnel, including by attempting to sink US warships in the Middle East and kill their crews, the WSJ reported, citing people familiar with the warnings.Iranian missiles came close to American warships during attacks in September. The Pentagon moved a dozen B-1 bombers from a British military base last week amid concerns that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was planning a drone attack.Meanwhile, Iran has intensified attacks on vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz, at least three commercial vessels were hit over the weekend. A drone attack also set fire to the Emirati tanker Petro Dolphin near Oman on Sunday, leaving two Indian sailors missing.The US military is preparing for a possible resumption of hostilities. A third aircraft carrier strike group and another Marine expeditionary unit are heading towards the Middle East, while the Pentagon is considering deploying additional air-defence equipment and munitions to regional bases, the WSJ reported.US president Donald Trump has ruled out attacking Iran before the November 3 midterm elections, but has publicly considered striking the country’s Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site. US officials have also said the military is preparing options for further strikes.Iran has used the pause in direct fighting to rebuild missile and drone facilities and replenish its arsenal. Satellite imagery shows that it has also strengthened defences around sensitive sites, including the Pickaxe Mountain and Natanz nuclear facilities.Iranian officials have also said the country’s airports, seaports and power plants have prepared for wartime conditions by installing shelters and backup supplies.Alongside these preparations, Tehran has stepped up efforts to mobilise domestic support. State media has broadcast pro-government rallies, while billboards in the capital advertise civilian training courses in the use of shoulder-fired anti-aircraft missiles and sniper rifles. The Revolutionary Guard has also publicised the training of female commando units and sent personnel to a kindergarten in northeastern Iran to recount stories of the earlier fighting.
Article Summary: Iran has strengthened defences around sensitive nuclear sites and stepped up efforts to rally domestic support. Tehran has also warned regional officials that a fresh conflict could spill across the Gulf. The warnings are part of Tehran’s effort to deter potential American attacks after November 3 midterm elections.

Article Title: BMC issues show-cause notice to Mumbai Coastal Road contractors over unauthorised debris use
Article Text:
BMC issues show-cause notice to Mumbai Coastal Road contractors





MUMBAI: Days after the BMC launched the Mumbai Debris Control and Tracking System (MDCTS) portal to track C&D waste from the site where it is generated to an authorised unloading site, the BMC has issued a show-cause notice to the contractors executing a package of the Mumbai Coastal Road (south) project over the alleged use of excavation material sourced from private construction sites without mandatory transportation permissions.The civic body has directed the Larsen & Toubro-HCC joint venture to stop backfilling work using unauthorised material until clearance is obtained from the civic administration. The contractor has been given 72 hours to explain why the material should not be removed at its cost and stringent action initiated against it.A senior BMC official said, “The objective is for BMC to improve accountability by linking construction and demolition waste from its source and upto its final destination.”Staring October 12, BMC has also begun imposing a ₹25,000 penalty per violation on vehicles transporting construction and excavation waste without an authorised, active tracking system.Meanwhile the notice follows a site inspection conducted by the BMC’s solid waste management department on October 1 at the coastal stretch between Haji Ali and PDP Garden. Officials found backfilling activity underway and, upon checking vehicle details and challans, found that the earth being used was reportedly being brought from private building construction sites across Mumbai.According to the notice, the developers and transporters concerned had not obtained the mandatory permission to transport excavation material from the BMC or the competent authority. The civic body said the use of material from unauthorised sources violated the tender conditions, which require filling material to be procured only from authorised quarries or approved sources with valid permissions.The notice cites violations of the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules of 2016 and 2025, directions of the Bombay high court concerning illegal transportation of earth and debris, and the project’s contractual conditions and technical specifications.The contractor has been asked to submit supporting documents, including details of the source of the material, valid transportation permissions, royalty challans and geotechnical test reports. It must also provide a statement of the material brought to the site, along with details of approved sources.BMC has warned that failure to submit a satisfactory reply within the stipulated period could lead to further action without additional notice. The civic body has also directed its officials to initiate action against private developers found transporting construction and demolition material without the required permission.A response from L & T spokesperson stated, “We have received the notice from the BMC’s Solid Waste Management department regarding the source of backfilling material at a section of the Mumbai Coastal Road project. Compliance with all applicable rules, permissions and contract conditions is a priority for us. We remain committed to resolving this matter promptly and to delivering the project to the required standards. ”
Article Summary: BMC issues show-cause notice to Mumbai Coastal Road contractors over alleged use of excavation material sourced from private construction sites. Larsen & Toubro- HCC joint venture directed to stop backfilling work using unauthorised material. The contractor has been given 72 hours to explain why the material should not be removed.

Article Title: ‘Sahil asked for a chance, told IIT-B won’t repeat mistake’: Police
Article Text:
Sahil Wakode was a second-year BTech student at IIT Bombay who died by suicide last month





MUMBAI: Sahil Wakode, the second-year BTech student at IIT Bombay who died by suicide last month, in his written statement to the institute after being caught copying, had said he would not repeat the mistake and had asked for a “chance”, police sources said.Wakode apologised and said it was a mistake and that he had not prepared well for the exam, they added. The police said they are carrying out a detailed probe based on this statement.Meanwhile, professor Suryanarayan Dolla, who has been named an accused in the abetment to suicide case, in his statement to the police, has denied allegations of harassment levelled against him by Wakode’s parents.Wakode (22) was found dead in his hostel room hours after the exam on Sept 18. The institute’s policy for handling academic malpractices mentions that a student who is caught copying is given two working days to submit a written response, after being given a copy of the report by the instructor and after the evidence is submitted.Immediately after he was caught copying, Wakode spoke to a female friend and told her his thermodynamics theory paper did not go well and he was worried as he had wanted to score well.He also told her that he had been caught cheating during the exam, police sources said.The city crime, probing the case, has already recorded the statement of IIT Bombay director Shireesh Kedare.Kedare said it is significant for understanding the standard operating procedure (SOP) for dealing with students caught copying using unauthorised material during examinations.Other than Prof Dolla, against whom allegations were levelled, police have recorded the statements of over 20 individuals so far, including 12 students.While the police probe is on, an internal inquiry by a 10-member committee set up by the institute is also underway. The institute’s guidelines state that “on discovery of an act of indiscipline during the exam, the invigilator should confiscate the relevant material like chits, phones, answer papers, give a fresh answerbook and students should be allowed to resume writing the exam”.A disciplinary action document passed by the institute’s senate in Aug this year, which called for a fail grade and a semester’s suspension for copying using chits, smartphones or other gadgets, has now been withdrawn.At a senate meeting held last week, the institute reverted to its 2015 punishment guidelines, which call for suspension only in serious cases, such as impersonation, or for repeat offences. In a revised SOP, the institute also included a provision for the invigilator to alert the wellness response team (WRT) for student support.Wakode was caught with his phone during the mid-semester exam on Sept 18. Hours after the incident, he was found dead in his hostel room.Protests erupted on the campus immediately after the news spread, but many discontinued them after the institute held an open house four days later. About 10-12 students are continuing their protests near the main gate.They are also on a relay hunger strike. The students have been demanding an external probe into the incident. Sahil’s parents, Ravindra and Sonali, too, are on hunger strike. Their protest, too, entered the 12th day on Monday. They are demanding the arrest of institute officials and justice for their son.
Article Summary: Sahil Wakode was a second-year BTech student at IIT Bombay who died by suicide last month. In his written statement to the institute after being caught copying, Wakode had said he would not repeat the mistake and had asked for a ‘chance’ Wakode (22) was found dead in his hostel room hours after the exam on Sept 18.

Article Title: Maharashtra man beats wife to death, walks into police station to confess
Article Text:
A man named Mukesh killed his wife, Rohini, during an argument (Representative image generated using AI)





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: A 50-year-old man allegedly beat his wife to death following an argument at their home in Maharashtra’s Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district before walking into a police station and confessing to the crime, police said.The incident took place around 5am on Monday in Kannad town, where the accused, Mukesh Kumbhakarna, allegedly assaulted his 44-year-old wife, Rohini, following a heated argument, an official said on Tuesday.The couple had been living in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for their children’s schooling and had recently returned to Kannad for the festive season, the official said.About an hour after the alleged assault, Kumbhakarna walked into Kannad city police station and confessed to killing his wife, the official said.The accused suspected his wife’s character and frequently quarrelled with her, the official added.A case has been registered against Kumbhakarna under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with murder. An investigation is underway, the official said.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Mukesh Kumbhakarna allegedly assaulted his 44-year-old wife, Rohini, following a heated argument. An hour after the alleged assault, he walked into Kannad city police station and confessed to killing his wife. The couple had been living in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for their children’s schooling.

Article Title: ‘Has hoisting the national flag become illegal?’: CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke on leaders’ detention near Jantar Mantar
Article Text:
The leaders were detained by Delhi Police after reaching Jantar Mantar despite heavy barricading and a strong security presence, the party said.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday questioned the detention of party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka near Jantar Mantar, asking whether waving the national flag had become a violation of the law.The leaders were detained by Delhi Police after reaching Jantar Mantar despite heavy barricading and a strong security presence, the party said.Dipke said other team members, including Ajinkya Shinde, had also been detained.“Has hoisting the national flag become a violation of the law? Our team, led by Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya Shinde, went to Jantar Mantar this morning and waved the Tricolour there. Since when has waving the Tricolour become a violation of the law?” Dipke told news agency PTI.Calling the detention unjustified, Dipke said anyone who considered waving the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar a violation of the law was “anti-national”.“Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and others accompanying them have been arrested for waving the Tricolour. Strictest possible action should be taken against this, because how can you arrest someone for waving the national flag?” he said.“What kind of country is this? What kind of rule is this? Since when has waving the Tricolour in our own country, India, become a violation of the law?” Dipke added, calling the incident “the biggest example of a dictatorial mindset”.Earlier In a post on X, Dipke also said the party members had reached Jantar Mantar early in the morning with the Tricolour before being picked up by Delhi Police.“Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police. Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya, along with other team members, have been detained. You cannot denotify the resistance, @narendramodi,” he wrote.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke questions detention of party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Dipke asks whether waving the national flag had become a violation of the law. The leaders were detained by Delhi Police after reaching Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: MSEDCL takes action against power theft in rural Jalna
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





In a major crackdown on power theft, MSEDCL has booked 54 people in four criminal cases in Jalna’s Ambad taluka after detecting the theft of 21,037 electricity units, causing a loss of nearly Rs 4.9 lakh to the utility.“From direct hooks on live wires to brazen meter tampering, the accused had been stealing power using different unethical ways. Such acts could cause electrocution, transformer blasts and blackouts for the entire area, besides harming the interests of consumers who pay their power bills diligently,” said Dnyaneshwar Ardad, public relations officer for MSEDCL’s Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar zone.Cases have been registered at Partur police station under section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003, which provides for penalties and imprisonment of up to three years.The raid was led by assistant engineer Laxman Punde under the supervision of executive engineer Vikas Alhat. MSEDCL officials said the anti-theft drive will continue.
Article Summary: MSEDCL has booked 54 people in four criminal cases in Jalna’s Ambad taluka. The theft of 21,037 electricity units, causing a loss of nearly Rs 4.9 lakh to the utility. The raid was led by assistant engineer Laxman Punde.

Article Title: ​Beed school ‘imported’ students to keep teachers on payroll; principal suspended
Article Text:
Zilla Parishad, Beed

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





An official inquiry has exposed what appears to be a calculated attempt by a reputed aided school in Beed to inflate enrolment and prevent teachers from being declared surplus. The inquiry has uncovered 94 dubious student entries and three fake admissions. The school principal has been suspended, and an FIR has also been ordered against him.The probe found that the school’s enrolment figures were artificially boosted by retaining students who were actually attending other schools, while three students from Uttarakhand were entered into the system despite not being regular admissions.“The inquiry found that the 94 extra students are actually studying in other schools but were retained on the school’s rolls. No admission forms, attendance sheets or other supporting documents were produced for them,” zilla parishad education officer Jayashree Chavan said.The discrepancies surfaced during a scrutiny of student records and govt databases. While the UDISE portal showed 1,262 students for 2026-27, the SARAL portal reflected only 1,168 students, exposing a gap of 94 students.Officials found that entries of three students were made on the UDISE portal on Oct 7, though their admission date was shown as Sept 28.During the inquiry, the principal reportedly admitted that the students were not admitted through the regular process and that he had merely “imported” their names into the system.Officials said the enrolment was allegedly inflated to prevent teachers from becoming excess under staffing norms. The exact number of surplus teachers is yet to be determined.The probe also pointed to serious procedural violations. Student entries were made directly through the principal’s central login without the mandatory physical verification by the centre head and block education officer.“Reports from these supervisory officers were not on file, pointing to negligence at multiple levels,” the inquiry report stated, indicating that accountability may extend beyond the principal.The inquiry team examined enrolment records from 2012-13 to 2026-27 and found that records had not been properly maintained during the period from 2020-21 to 2023-24, when the current principal was in charge.“Following the findings, we directed immediate suspension of the principal, to which the school management complied. An order for registering an FIR against the principal is also issued,” Chavan said.The inquiry committee has recommended stricter checks, including mandatory physical verification by centre heads and block education officers before student data is approved on the Shalarth and SARAL portals.
Article Summary: An official inquiry has exposed what appears to be a calculated attempt by a reputed aided school in Beed to inflate enrolment. The inquiry has uncovered 94 dubious student entries and three fake admissions. The school principal has been suspended, and an FIR has also been ordered against him.

Article Title: Five decades on, Maharashtra’s Irrigation Act remains toothless for want of rules
Article Text:
The issue has assumed greater urgency amid a worsening drought situation

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The Maharashtra Irrigation Act, 1976, has remained without statutory rules for nearly five decades in a striking case of administrative neglect, rendering several key provisions ineffective even as the state grapples with recurring drought.The Act empowers govt to curb or ban water-intensive crops like sugar cane during periods of acute water scarcity. It also authorises canal officers to arrest water thieves without a warrant, seize pumps, cut electricity supplies, impose fines and prosecute those tampering with irrigation infrastructure.Water management expert and retired Water and Land Management Institute (WALMI)associate professor Madhav Purandare said the absence of implementing rules had created a regulatory vacuum, fuelling widespread water theft, vandalism and arbitrary decision-making. “Failure to frame rules is not merely an administrative lapse but a systemic violation of constitutional intent. While the legislature lays down broad principles, rules determine how, when and to whom water rights are allocated. Without them, discretion runs unchecked,” he said.In the absence of a legal framework under the 1976 law, the water resources department continues to rely selectively on the outdated Bombay Canal Rules, 1934, framed under the repealed Bombay Irrigation Act of 1879.Purandare alleged that the vacuum had enabled politically influential irrigators to corner water resources, leaving tail-end farmers deprived. “Powerful vote-bank interests capture the bulk of available water while vulnerable farming communities are left high and dry,” he said.The issue has assumed greater urgency amid a worsening drought situation. With drought declared in 265 of Maharashtra’s 358 talukas, covering nearly 74% of the state, and local bodies ordered to reduce water supply by 10% ahead of summer, experts warned that the lack of enforceable irrigation rules had left agricultural regions exposed to water hoarding and inequitable distribution.Calling it a case of “institutional lawlessness”, Purandare said the continued failure to notify rules effectively undermined Constitution by preventing legal accountability. “Nothing is legally committed, nothing can legally be challenged, creating space for unchecked privatisation and misuse,” he warned.A public interest litigation (PIL) filed by Purandare led Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court in Aug 2015to direct state govt to set a timeline for finalising the rules. Although an expert committee submitted draft rules on July 28, 2015, they remain pending more than a decade later.Water rights activist Abhijeet Dhanorkar said the delay had weakened Maharashtra’s ability to tackle drought. “The Maharashtra Irrigation Act was intended to be the backbone of water governance. More than half of the state’s sugar cane is grown in dam command areas and consumes nearly 70% of stored dam water. Sections 47 and 48 allow restrictions on water-intensive crops during scarcity, while Section 49 allows suspension of water supply. These provisions have never been invoked because rules were never framed,” he said.Repeated attempts to contact water resources minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil for comment were unsuccessful till going to the press.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Irrigation Act, 1976, has remained without statutory rules for nearly five decades. The Act empowers govt to curb or ban water-intensive crops like sugar cane during periods of acute water scarcity. It also authorises canal officers to arrest water thieves without a warrant.
